I had a feeling this question would be asked.

Images would be very difficult to circumvent with reverse image searching. The image would have to be severely altered to not match against a reverse image search.

Links to websites are very easy to deal with as well. Even if someone is attempting to use a service like tinyurl to obfuscate the link. The link would redirect to the same endpoint.

The thing that would be difficult is videos, even those could technically be reversed search. However I'm not aware of a service that does this currently open to the public.

Definitely an interesting question.

For me, I have to admit, even though I enjoy lots and lots of instrumental music, I tend to prefer more music with singing and lyrics. I've always considered music as a method to convey human emotions to the listener. Singing is one of the most efficient instruments for that, since humans are practically learning to interpret emotions from human voices from the moment they are born.

Couple of examples where the vocals really add to the song:

Björk - It's oh so quiet

The song succeeds so well in conveying the emotional rollercoaster that happens when a person falls in love. I can't imagine how a story like this could have been done without the aid of Björk's vocal delivery.

Bright Eyes - A spindle, a darkness, a fever, and a necklace

In this song the vocals bring a whole new level of desperation to the song. It wouldn't have near the emotional impact it has without the vocals and lyrics.

Of course there are songs where vocals basically ruin everything, but I guess same could be said of any instrument.

Then again, as with all music and arts, everything comes down to personal preference. This is just how I view it.
